text:
Buffalo's season has been a struggle, and Tage Thompson has been the reason it isn't worse. The Athletic's Matthew Fairburn put it plainly: Thompson is "the guy dragging them into games," and "more guys need to come along for the ride." He leads our whole league in wins added by goals this season.

The numbers are huge. Seventeen goals and 30 points in 25 games, a five-game point streak, and a shot that tops out above 100 mph, top percentile in the league. He is playing with Jiri Kulich and Zach Benson on a top line the Buffalo papers say has revived Kulich, and our season-end range runs from 40 to 57 goals.

Here is the honest part. He has 17 goals on 11.4 expected, shooting 18% against 15% last season, and the Sabres have scored ten more goals than expected with him on the ice. We flag him as due to cool. But his own chances are real and rising, at 1.39 expected goals per 60, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 93rd percentile for chances from in front of the net last season. Buffalo's problem is everyone else.
headline: Tage Thompson keeps dragging Buffalo along
